topics.label: Outland Sponsorship
topics.metaDescription: Outland sponsorship process for couples applying while the sponsored partner is abroad — timeline, visa office routing, and travel rules.
topics.lead: Outland sponsorship is filed while the sponsored spouse or partner is living outside Canada. It's processed through the visa office responsible for their region, and in some cases can move faster than an inland application.

topics.label: Inland Sponsorship
topics.metaDescription: Inland sponsorship for couples where the partner is already in Canada — open work permit eligibility and travel restrictions explained.
topics.lead: Inland sponsorship is filed while the sponsored spouse or partner is already living in Canada, generally on valid temporary status. It's the route that allows an accompanying open work permit application while the sponsorship itself is processed.

topics.label: Spousal Open Work Permit
topics.seoTitle: Spousal Open Work Permit Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Spousal open work permit eligibility for inland sponsorship applicants — timing, processing, and what it authorizes.
topics.lead: A spousal open work permit lets a sponsored partner work for almost any Canadian employer while their inland sponsorship application is being processed, rather than waiting without authorization for the sponsorship decision itself.

topics.label: Family Sponsorship (overview, all categories)
topics.seoTitle: Family Sponsorship Canada 2026: Spouse, Parent & Child | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Spousal, parent/grandparent, and dependent-child sponsorship routes explained. Inland vs outland, PGP lottery, and income requirements. Free assessment.
topics.lead: Spousal, parent/grandparent, and dependent-child sponsorship each carry different eligibility rules, but every stream is ultimately assessed on whether the relationship is genuine and the sponsor can meet the financial undertaking required.

topics.label: Dependent Child Sponsorship
topics.metaDescription: Sponsor a dependent child for Canadian PR — age and dependency criteria, and how this pairs with a parent's own application.
topics.lead: Dependent child sponsorship allows Canadian citizens and permanent residents to sponsor their children for permanent residence, based on age and dependency criteria assessed at the time of application.

topics.label: Adopted Child Sponsorship
topics.metaDescription: Sponsor an adopted child for Canadian permanent residence — the two adoption pathways and what documentation each requires.
topics.lead: Canadian citizens and permanent residents can sponsor an adopted child for permanent residence, generally through one of two routes: sponsorship as a family member, or a citizenship grant through adoption, depending on the sponsor's status and the adoption's circumstances.

topics.label: Parents & Grandparents Program (PGP)
topics.metaDescription: PGP lottery process, income requirements, and the Super Visa alternative for sponsoring parents and grandparents. Free eligibility review.
topics.lead: The PGP is the dedicated pathway for Canadian citizens and permanent residents to sponsor their parents or grandparents for permanent residence. Because demand consistently exceeds the annual intake, IRCC selects sponsors through a randomized interest-to-sponsor process rather than first-come, first-served.

topics.label: PGP Invitation to Apply
topics.seoTitle: PGP Invitation to Apply Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: What happens after PGP lottery selection: the invitation window, required documents, and the full application timeline.
topics.lead: Being selected in the Parents and Grandparents Program's interest-to-sponsor lottery isn't approval — it's an invitation to submit a complete application within a set deadline, which is then independently assessed on its own merits.
